catalog.description: Vac-rated fatigues and a web harness are the fleet infantry working uniform. They preserve unrestricted movement but leave the wearer dangerously exposed in a firefight.
Charcoal laminate protects the torso and major joints without becoming a walking bulkhead. It accepts a modest mobility penalty for dependable line protection.
Navy reconnaissance plate uses overlapping segments and a low-profile sensor hood. It keeps a scout fast and elusive while stopping fragments and glancing fire.
Crimson assault plate layers dense ceramic and powered bracing over every vital zone. It survives severe punishment, but its mass is obvious in every movement.
Outlaw plate combines cut-down security armor, ship plating, and hand-fitted seals. No two suits agree, but the better examples are quick and stubborn.
Army-green line armor favors interchangeable plates and field-serviceable joints. It is heavier than scout gear and built for days away from a proper armory.
A militia kit combines a torso plate, helmet, and local impact layers. It protects a section leader from fragments but cannot replace full combat armor.
